observations: Photo 0: a yellow steel household gas cylinder with a carry collar, valve fitted, paint worn and spotted, a gas shop sticker with a phone number on the collar and handwritten marks; stamped collar text not legible.
Photos 1 and 2: a different cylinder, blue, shorter and wider, with a FERADISCO logo on the body (photo 1), worn black edge on the collar ring, paint chipped, brass valve fitted with no regulator.
So two different cylinders appear in one listing; it is not clear which one, or whether both, are for sale.
Both are the size of a standard household cooking gas cylinder judged against the floor tiles; no capacity or tare weight stamp is readable.
No dents or bulges visible in view; light surface rust on the blue collar ring and base, base not shown close up.
Dealer watermark PETRONJAY BUSINESS, posted on Jiji.

read_from: photos 0 to 2 cylinder shape and size against floor tiles; capacity stamp not legible

claims.evidence: Size looks like a standard household cylinder in photos 0 to 2, but no capacity or tare weight stamp is readable on the collar.
Photos 0 to 2 show ordinary steel LPG cylinders with collar and valve.

risks.proof: Close-up of the stamped collar showing capacity and tare weight
risks.if_unproven: as the smaller common household size

risks.proof: Clip of a soapy water leak test on the valve with the cylinder holding gas

risks.risk: Rust or dents at the base weakening the shell
risks.proof: Photo of the underside and foot ring

risks.risk: Unclear which of the two cylinders is sold, and whether it comes with gas
risks.proof: Seller confirms which cylinder, with one photo of it on a scale showing its weight
risks.if_unproven: as the more worn cylinder, sold empty

proof_requests: Close-up of the stamped collar showing capacity, tare weight and test date
Confirm which cylinder is for sale, with a photo of it on a scale
Photo of the underside and foot ring
Clip of a soapy water leak test on the valve
response.reason: A household cooking gas cylinder is a plain good identified by type and the size seen fits the claimed 12.5kg, so it can be priced at its worst case as an empty, worn cylinder, with the capacity stamp and leak test as the proof that would raise it.
